content.text: When digital creators in Bangladesh cannot rely on Stripe or PayPal, they're left with a critical infrastructure problem: securing a payment system that respects their sovereignty. The illusion of a 'workaround' is just that – an illusion. The real challenge lies in deploying a commerce stack that doesn't rely on foreign gatekeepers. The COREMERCH Sovereign Stack offers a solution, but which deployment option is right for you? Let's examine the differences between each choice.
What Each Option Actually Offers

The COREMERCH Sovereign Stack offers two primary deployment options: The Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) and The Edge Commerce Stack ($197). The Sovereign Starter Stack provides a basic commerce infrastructure with GitHub Pages for hosting, Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. On the other hand, The Edge Commerce Stack offers a more advanced commerce infrastructure with Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. The Edge Commerce Stack also includes SPF/DKIM/DMARC configuration, end-to-end testing, and additional features to enhance the overall user experience.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

One of the key differences between the two deployment options is how they handle restricted countries. The Sovereign Starter Stack relies on GitHub Pages for hosting, which may not be suitable for users in restricted countries. In contrast, The Edge Commerce Stack uses Cloudflare Pages for hosting, which offers better performance and more flexible hosting options, including support for restricted countries. Additionally, The Edge Commerce Stack includes more advanced features to help users comply with local regulations and minimize the risk of platform suspension.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, both deployment options offer competitive rates. NOWPayments charges a flat fee of 0.5% per transaction, making it an attractive option for digital creators who value simplicity and transparency. However, users in restricted countries may face higher fees due to local payment processing requirements. In contrast, The Edge Commerce Stack offers more advanced payment processing features, including support for multiple payment gateways and more flexible fee structures.
A wallet you control cannot be frozen by anyone — that is the fundamental difference from a platform account balance.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Ownership, automation, and delivery are critical components of any commerce infrastructure. The COREMERCH Sovereign Stack offers complete ownership of the storefront code, customer list, order history, product files, and wallet addresses. The Edge Commerce Stack also includes advanced automation features, including automatic on-chain crypto payment verification and instant product delivery. This ensures that users have complete control over their commerce infrastructure and can scale their business with confidence.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

So, which architecture to choose based on your situation? If you're a digital creator in Bangladesh who values simplicity and affordability, The Sovereign Starter Stack may be the better choice. However, if you're looking for more advanced features and flexibility, The Edge Commerce Stack is likely the better option. Additionally, users in restricted countries may want to consider The Edge Commerce Stack due to its more flexible hosting options and advanced payment processing features.
What does sovereign commerce infrastructure mean for digital creators?

The question of whether to build on platforms or build sovereign infrastructure comes down to a single risk calculation: what happens when the platform changes its terms, restricts your market, or suspends your account? For creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, and dozens of other restricted markets, that question has already been answered — the platform already said no. Sovereign infrastructure is not a backup plan for when platforms fail. It is the primary architecture for creators who cannot afford to depend on platforms that have already demonstrated they will exclude your market without notice, without recourse, and without apology. You own the store. You own the customer list. You own the revenue. No decision made in a boardroom in San Francisco can change any of that.
No KYC means no geographic gatekeeping — anyone in the world can pay you without creating an account or verifying identity.

After the stack is deployed under your accounts, no platform decision affects your revenue, your customer list, or your product delivery. Your Deployment Checklist

Audit your current infrastructure dependencies before building the sovereign stack — list every platform account your income depends on and identify the failure mode for each. For each platform that holds funds or controls access to customers, build the sovereign alternative in parallel before migrating. Start with the payment layer: NOWPayments configured with your self-custody wallet addresses. Then the backend: Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script handling webhook receipt and order processing. Then the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages serving your product pages. Then the data layer: Supabase or Google Sheets storing every order independently of any payment platform. Test the complete pipeline on mainnet. Migrate your audience to the sovereign store gradually — announce it to your existing audience as an upgrade, not a replacement.
COREMERCH has no access after deployment — the store runs under your accounts whether COREMERCH exists or not.
